summary: I pass on everything here. The game side is close: the books make Milwaukee a small favorite, with a de-vigged chance of 0.5305, and the data gives me real arguments on both sides without a clear winner. Milwaukee has the far better season record and the better last ten, but Tampa Bay's starter Griffin Jax has the better ERA and has allowed no earned runs over his last three starts, while Dustin May's recent ERA is 8.5909 with short outings. That split is exactly what a near coin-flip price should already reflect, so I see no reason to call the market wrong. The run line and total sit near their fair numbers too, and the total has the book split almost evenly between over and under. The player props are the weakest part: the newest quotes are old, most props have only a few books or just two, and nothing in the data gives a hitter-specific read beyond the price itself. Missing inputs that matter are matchup history, team totals and standings. Without them I would rather say the market is probably right than force a bet.
